k perfect and the irreducible components of D_red regular

k finite, p-adic, or algebraically closed; m invertible in k; p not dividing m when k is p-adic
X integral, regular in codimension one, D effective Cartier; complete for parts (2) and (3) of Theorem 1.5

quantifier_and_regularity_points: Dimension restrictions are part of the statements and must not be normalized away: 1.2 and 1.6 allow d >= 0 (lines 227, 371), while 3.5 requires d >= 1 (line 1180) and 8.3 is stated for d >= 1 with induction starting at d <= 2 (lines 2697-2698, 2727).

The divisor in 1.1 and 3.5 is reduced effective Cartier (lines 211-212, 1180-1181); in 1.2 it need only be effective Cartier with regular reduced components (lines 1511-1512); 6.4 allows an arbitrary effective Cartier divisor (lines 2068-2069).

Coefficient regimes are not interchangeable: Z[1/p] when p > 1, and Z/m with m in k^x in characteristic zero (lines 375-377, 2871-2875). The restatement 4.5 writes R = [1/p] at line 1518 whereas the introduction writes Z[1/p] at line 233, a literal notational difference in the source.
Conditional dependence on resolution of singularities appears in the definition of Lambda (lines 493-494) and in the second half of the proof of 3.5 (lines 1228-1230).
The double S_X is formed for integral regular quasi-projective X and effective Cartier D (lines 821-825); later uses take X smooth projective and D reduced (lines 1115-1116).

The normalization and its projective normal compactification are fixed data in the definition of Suslin homology (lines 632-640); the remark that C_infty is treated as a reduced Cartier divisor at line 633 must be preserved.

In the reduction of 1.1(2) the specific plane curve is the one with homogeneous equation $x_0x^2_1-x^3_2 = 0$ (lines 1421-1423); the computation must keep this exact equation and the stated groups Omega_k + Z versus Z.

In the definition of the EKW group the two relation types are (c1) f in O^x_{C^N, nu^*(D)} with f(x) = 1 for all x in nu^*(D), and (c2) C an snc subcurve with f in O^x_{C, C cap D} (lines 2839-2846); both quantifiers are needed for the comparison.

The moving-lemma embedding-dimension inequalities in 8.3 are explicit numeric conditions: edim(C') = 2 < dim(Y'), edim(C' cap Y_i) + dim(C cap Y_i) <= 1 < dim(Y_i) for every other irreducible component, and the analogous inequality for components of D' (lines 2757-2765).
The degree of the alteration in 6.1 and 6.2 is a power of the exponential characteristic, and the resulting map h' is finite flat of that same degree (lines 1899-1901, 1965-1972, 2009-2010).

No limit process or completed object is introduced; the only 'limiting' step is the algebraic fact that a divisible torsion group of bounded exponent vanishes (lines 1225-1226), with bound exponent (d-1)! (lines 1209-1211).
core_recount_boundaries: In the introduction, 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.5 and 1.6 are announcement statements; their proofs appear later as 4.3 plus 4.4, 4.5, 5.4, 6.3-6.5, and 8.4. Announcements are not counted again as separate cores.
4.5 (thm:M1) is existing record 2091 and is not re-counted as a new candidate; the introduction statement 1.2 is likewise not counted.

6.3 and 6.4 are direct applications of 6.2 with localization sequences and of 1.2, so they are not separate cores. 6.5 is a comparison assembled by the same hypersurface induction used inside 4.1 and 8.3 and is not counted separately.
7.7 (snc-surface) is a genuine surface-only moving lemma, but its construction is generalized and subsumed by 8.3; counting both would double-count one geometric core, so only 8.3 is retained.

4.1 and 4.2 are supporting torsion statements with proofs inside the work; they feed 4.3 and are not independently retained because their mechanism is the double comparison already retained as 3.5 plus cited torsion theorems.

Cited results with no author proof are never counted: thm:suslinhomology (Schmidt), the motivic Hom identification in Section 2 (Kelly-Pedicchio), lem:LW-lci* (Krishna), and the items listed inside lem:comparisonLWlci.

Weak forms and direct corollaries are not split: cor:Main-8, remk:SS, the Russell Chow group consequences at lines 1493-1504, and the EKW presentation remark at lines 396-399 are applications, not new cores.

No candidate is proposed for the surface case of 8.3, for the d=2 seed in 5.4, or for the smooth projective finiteness lemma 6.1 taken alone; each is an input or a special case, not an independent second core.
